Examining more of the store to identify the tables affected by DeleteMemo.

DeleteMemo directly deletes from the memo table. It explicitly cascades through memo_relation and attachment via DeleteMemoRelation and ListAttachments. The memo_share table also has a schema-level ON DELETE CASCADE on memo_id. Whether schema-level cascades count as explicit cascade code is still unclear.

Schema-level ON DELETE CASCADE is implicit, not explicit. The affected tables are memo, memo_relation, and attachment.

API-level DeleteMemo also removes comment memos from the memo table. Reactions and inbox entries are not explicitly cascaded; reactions would be orphaned since the reaction table has no foreign key to memo. The latest schema shows neither memo_relation nor attachment has foreign key constraints.

SQLite has foreign keys disabled. This means cascade deletions will not propagate automatically through the schema.

The `memo` table is directly affected. `memo_relation` and `attachment` are reached only through explicit cascade code in `store.DeleteMemo`. Postgres and MySQL would trigger automatic cascades on `memo_share`, but SQLite does not.

`memo_share` is excluded from the explicit cascade path. It is only touched by schema-level `ON DELETE CASCADE`, which fails on SQLite because foreign keys are disabled. The three tables always affected by `DeleteMemo` are `memo`, `memo_relation`, and `attachment`.

Reaction rows are not deleted by DeleteMemo. Cache invalidation in store.go was checked but found no extra table effects.

The phrase "explicit cascade code" is ambiguous. It could mean only the Go application-level cleanup, or the SQL schema CASCADE as well. Similar evaluation questions typically expect tracing every table touched by a function, including both direct SQL and application-level cascades.

The full set of affected tables is memo, memo_relation, attachment, and memo_share. The parenthetical phrase is meant to ensure all related tables are counted, not merely the primary memo row. SQL ON DELETE CASCADE counts as explicit cascade code, so memo_share is included alongside the Go-level cleanup.
